subject: Climate & Environment
title: Why Insects Matter Most
description: Learn Why Insects Matter Most in one minute.

hook.text: If all humans vanished, Earth would flourish. If all insects vanished, most life would collapse.

buildup.text: Insects pollinate 75% of crops, decompose waste, and feed birds, bats, and fish.

discovery.text: A German study found flying insect biomass dropped 76% in protected areas over 27 years.

twist.text: Pesticides, habitat loss, and light pollution are driving what scientists call an 'insect apocalypse.'

climax.text: Without insect pollinators, one-third of the food we eat would simply vanish from farms.

punchline.text: The tiny creatures we ignore hold the whole system together.

quiz.question: What percentage of crops depend on insect pollinators?

details.summary: Insects represent over 80 percent of all known animal species and perform irreplaceable roles in pollination, decomposition, soil health, and as food for birds and fish. Recent studies suggest insect biomass has declined 75 percent in some regions over 30 years.
details.whyItMatters: Insect decline threatens the ecological foundation that supports all terrestrial life. Because insects are small and often disliked, their crisis receives far less attention than mammal or bird losses.
takeaways: Insects pollinate, decompose waste, and feed countless other species
German studies found a 75 percent decline in insect biomass since 1989
Light pollution, pesticides, and habitat loss are major drivers

faq.question: Why is the insect decline called an ecological apocalypse?
faq.answer: Insects underpin nearly every food web on land. Their loss cascades upward to birds, bats, fish, and amphibians that depend on them for food, and downward to plants that rely on them for pollination and decomposition.

faq.question: What can individuals do to help insect populations?
faq.answer: Plant native wildflowers, reduce pesticide use, leave garden areas wild, turn off unnecessary outdoor lights at night, and avoid manicured lawns in favor of diverse plantings that provide year-round food and shelter.
